record: AISEF V2 — ROADMAP-2.2 WAVE-2 lane Findings (owner item 4): analysis only; the kernel is frozen and no kernel code is changed here. Each item is for an owner remediation decision.

findings.title: os.kill(pid, 0) is a killing call on Windows, not an existence probe
findings.severity: latent (not reachable by any claimed/tested path today; reachable by a real `aisef run` on Windows)
findings.site: aisef2/app/client.py:46, _is_gone() — the escapee existence probe called from _release_session() on a RangeEscaped teardown
findings.intended_behavior: _is_gone is a PURE existence probe: its docstring states 'Never signals the process: signal 0 only asks whether the pid exists for us', and the module header says 'Nothing is ever signalled here'. This is the range teardown contract (P4-LIFETIME-SEMANTICS §3) and INV-MUTATION-AUTHORITY: a probe must never expand into a signal.
findings.actual_on_windows: CPython maps os.kill(pid, sig) on Windows, for any sig other than CTRL_C_EVENT/CTRL_BREAK_EVENT, to OpenProcess + TerminateProcess(handle, sig). So os.kill(pid, 0) on a LIVE pid calls TerminateProcess(handle, 0): it TERMINATES the process (exit code 0) and returns success. _is_gone then returns False ('cannot prove gone -> alive'), so the caller both KILLED the escapee and reported it still alive — an unauthorized signal from a probe, violating the stated invariant.

reachability_analysis.range_has_a_windows_path: yes — ProcessRange uses _Job (a Windows Job Object) where POSIX uses _Posix (aisef2/runtime/process_range.py).
reachability_analysis.process_table_on_windows: process_table() is '/proc on Linux, ps elsewhere' (process_range.py:117-119); Windows has no `ps`, so _ps_table() raises, _is_gone catches it (present=None) and ALWAYS falls through to the os.kill branch — so on Windows the hazard is the common path, not an edge.
reachability_analysis.exercised_today: NO. The range/escapee tests are @skipUnless(posix) so they never run on the Windows CI leg; the wheel/product smoke runs only on ubuntu; `aisef run` is documented for Linux and macOS (docs/v2/USAGE.md). So no claimed or tested path reaches it.
reachability_analysis.real_risk: a user who runs `aisef run` on Windows and whose session process escapes its Job Object range and is seen alive at release would have it TerminateProcess'd by the teardown probe — an unauthorized kill, and a mis-report ('alive' after killing it).

findings.proposed_remediation_NOT_APPLIED: Guard the probe by platform: on POSIX keep os.kill(pid, 0); on Windows replace it with a non-killing existence check (OpenProcess(SYNCHRONIZE|PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION) + GetExitCodeProcess via ctypes, treating STILL_ACTIVE as alive and a closed/absent handle as gone) — never TerminateProcess. Alternatively, make the escapee path POSIX-only and have the Windows Job Object teardown carry its own non-killing liveness check. Either is a kernel change; the kernel is frozen, so this awaits an owner decision.

findings.title: freeze_manifest V2_007 promoted_from.sha256 does not match the dossier's _lf_sha
findings.status: OPEN (carried from wave 1; no change here)
findings.detail: The V2_007 freeze-manifest exception records a promoted_from.sha256 that differs from the dossier's LF-normalized sha (_lf_sha). It is a provenance-record drift, not a product defect.
findings.remediation_plan: Re-derive the two shas on this tree, confirm which is the authentic LF-normalized digest of the promoted source, and correct the stale field with an append-only correction record (never rewrite the sealed manifest). Prepare the evidence (both digests + the bytes they are over) for owner review before any edit. No reseal without separate owner approval.
